text:
Sarah Nguyen: heads-up — mkdocs build on branch 'notebook-migrate' fails during linkcheck. Anchors that should resolve after code blocks are 404'ing.

docs-ci: Build failed: linkcheck step — job #4523

Jordan Patel: can you paste the markdown snippet that's producing the anchor? Last time it was a fenced block right after a heading.

Sarah Nguyen: failing excerpt from docs/guide/advanced.md:

```markdown
### JSON Output
```json
{"result": "ok"}
```

When the linkcheck looks for docs/guide/advanced.md#json-output it can't find the fragment.

Leo Kim: looks like mkdocs slugify is treating something differently — if there's a fenced block immediately after the heading mkdocs sometimes drops the header from the TOC. Quick workaround: add an explicit id `### JSON Output {#json-output}` or insert a blank line before the code fence.

Maria Ortiz: adding explicit ids feels safest for migration. Also we should update any cross-page refs to use the explicit id.

Jordan Patel: alternative is to normalize via a small script that post-processes headings during migration. But explicit ids are quicker.

Sarah Nguyen: i'll open a tiny PR with explicit ids and fix up the one or two broken links. @Jordan can you run the linkcheck locally when I'm done? I'll post the PR link here.

Jordan Patel: running `mkdocs build --strict --linkcheck` locally now.

refs: none needed here

docs-ci: PR 789 opened by Sarah Nguyen: "explicit-heading-ids-for-json-output-fix" — CI pending

Leo Kim: if we keep seeing duplicates, we should add a linter rule to flag duplicate slugs during CI.

Maria Ortiz: :thumbsup: i'll add a note to the migration checklist so authors remember to add `{#explicit-id}` when moving notebooks.

Sarah Nguyen: PR created and pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 — tests passed locally for me.

Jordan Patel: local linkcheck passes for me too. Approving.

Leo Kim: LGTM

docs-ci: PR merged and staging deploy started — build 4524
